newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold rebounds to end higher after two-way trade.
newsitem.headline: HK gold rebounds to end higher after two-way trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold rebounded during afternoon trade on Tuesday to end the day above New York's Monday close after busy two-way trade, bullion dealers said.
"We're seeing both buying and selling in a very, very active market," said Swiss Bank Corp chief dealer Anderson Cheung just before the market closed at 1630 (0830 GMT).
Hong Kong gold finished at US$368.80/369.30 per ounce, up from New York's Monday close at $368.00/50, after dipping as low as $367.50/80 in the morning, dealers said.
Some said traders who had established short positions earlier were covering their positions in afternoon trade.
Other dealers reported fresh buying interest from Europe later in the day, particularly from London and Switzerland.
One trader at an international bank said the market had also seen bargain hunting after the price dipped to $367.90 in morning trade, but did not specify origins.
Several dealers reported their lowest trades in the morning at $367.50/80, but said that level was touched only briefly.
Hong Kong spot gold prices slid past $368 per ounce largely on fund and producer selling, traders said.
Local gold ended HK$8 lower at HK$3,410 a tael. Physical demand had perked up, but not as much as expected, dealers said.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +5.00 from -1.05 at its previous fix.
